research_insight_text_link.research_insight_description: Commonwealth Fusion Systems is researching and developing high field superconducting magnets and tokamak fusion subsystems. Work such as grooved, stacked plate superconducting magnets and apparatus, magnet, and method of manufacture targets robust, modular HTS coils, while techniques for distributing forces in high field magnets and high temperature superconductor magnets with quench damage resiliency address mechanical and thermal reliability. Additional efforts include tritium shunt heat exchangers with sweep gas and tritium injection techniques for fuel handling.

overview_description.description: Commonwealth Fusion Systems develops fusion energy systems using high-temperature superconducting (HTS) magnets to create compact tokamak reactors. It is building SPARC, a demonstration device designed to achieve net energy gain from fusion and laying the groundwork for ARC, a grid-connected fusion power plant targeting early 2030s operation. The company partners with MIT and manufactures its HTS magnets and related components, applying peer-reviewed science in its firewalling of plasma and reactor engineering. It has introduced innovations like the PIT VIPER superconducting cable to support pulsed-power magnet systems and accelerate readiness for commercial fusion.
